newsitem.title: USA: DT says adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: DT says adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: DT Industries on Tuesday said it adopted a shareholder rights plan.

"While the company did not take this action in response to any known effort to acquire control of DT, the board felt it prudent and in the best interest of shareholders to establish a rights plan," said chief executive Stephen Gore.

A dividend of one preferred stock purchase right has been declared for each outstanding share of common stock to shareholders of record on September 2, said the maker of automated production systems and metal components.
The rights will not be exercisable until a person or group acquires, or commences a tender offer to acquire, ownership of more than 15 percent of DT's common stock, the company said.
Each right, when exercisable, entitles the holder to purchase one one-hundredth of a share of Series A preferred stock at $130, subject to adjustment, DT said.

Upon acquisition of 15 percent of DT's common stock without consent of the board, rights holders, except for the acquiring person, may purchase at the exercised price, common stock having a value equal to two times the exercise price of the right. In case of a merger or other combination in which DT is not the surviving entity, or if 50 percent or more of DT's assets or earning power are sold, rights holders may receive, upon exercise, common stock of the acquiror.
Prior to becoming exercisable, the rights are redeemable by the board of directors for $0.01 per right. If not so redeemed, the rights will expire on September 4, 2007.
